# Product experience and design

<!-- Generated by scripts/package/render_roles.py. Edit the YAML source, not this file. -->

**Department id:** `design`  
**Mission:** Make the product usable, accessible, intentional in appearance and faithful in implementation.

## Startup stage

One product designer covers UX, UI and a small token set; accessibility and design QA are checklists the designer and engineer share. The states matrix and token file are the two artefacts never to skip.

## Agents operating in this department

`design-lead`, `ux-designer`, `ui-designer`, `design-systems-engineer`, `accessibility-specialist`, `design-qa-auditor`

## Roles

### UX and interaction designer

Role id: `ux-designer`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Make critical tasks completable and recoverable on every device before visual design. |
| Scope of responsibility | Flows, information architecture, wireframes, interaction models, states. |
| Core activities | Map flows including failure and recovery; Build IA; Wireframe critical paths; Specify states and keyboard behaviour |
| Inputs | PRD; Research findings; Platform constraints |
| Outputs and deliverables | User flows; IA; Wireframes; States matrix; Interaction specs |
| Decisions it can make | Flow and IA proposals |
| Decisions requiring approval | Design lead |
| Collaborating roles | product; ux-research; engineering |
| Reporting relationship | design-lead |
| KPIs | Task completion in tests; States specified (%) |
| Quality expectations | All states; navigation from user goals; no template start |
| Tools and resources | States matrix template; IA template |
| Common failure modes | Beautiful but unusable; Missing error and empty states |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | None beyond lead |

### UI and visual designer

Role id: `ui-visual-designer`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Give the product an intentional visual language appropriate to its audience. |
| Scope of responsibility | Visual direction, screens, responsive layouts, motion, micro-interactions. |
| Core activities | Choose and justify direction; Design hierarchy and rhythm; Specify responsive and motion behaviour; Compare against patterns |
| Inputs | Wireframes; Brandbook; Tokens |
| Outputs and deliverables | Visual direction; High-fidelity screens; Responsive and motion specs |
| Decisions it can make | Visual proposals |
| Decisions requiring approval | Design lead and brand director |
| Collaborating roles | branding; design systems; frontend |
| Reporting relationship | design-lead |
| KPIs | Design QA pass rate; Distinctiveness review |
| Quality expectations | Every decorative element has a job; realistic content |
| Tools and resources | Design rationale template |
| Common failure modes | Generic SaaS layout; Purple gradients and glass cards by default; Fake dashboard data |

### Design systems designer/engineer

| Tools and resources | Token schema |

| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |

### Accessibility specialist

Role id: `accessibility-specialist`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Ensure WCAG 2.2 AA conformance with evidence. |
| Scope of responsibility | Design and implementation review, manual and automated testing, remediation guidance. |
| Core activities | Review contrast; structure; labels; focus; keyboard; targets; motion; Run automated and manual tests; Specify fixes and retest |
| Inputs | Designs; Rendered UI; Tokens |
| Outputs and deliverables | Accessibility review; Test report with per-criterion results |
| Decisions it can make | Conformance findings |
| Decisions requiring approval | Deviations need design lead and human owner with justified alternative |
| Collaborating roles | design; frontend; qa |
| Reporting relationship | design-lead |
| KPIs | Criteria passing; Issues fixed before release |
| Quality expectations | Automated plus manual; NOT_TESTED never shown as pass |
| Tools and resources | WCAG 2.2 AA checklist |
| Common failure modes | Scan-only conformance claims; Silent waivers |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Deviations |

### Design quality assurance

Role id: `design-qa`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Verify implemented UI matches the spec in behaviour, accessibility and appearance. |
| Scope of responsibility | Screenshot comparison, state checks, responsive and interaction checks. |
| Core activities | Compare rendered UI to spec at representative viewports; Check states and interactions; Log findings with evidence |
| Inputs | Spec; Tokens; Rendered UI |
| Outputs and deliverables | Design QA report |
| Decisions it can make | Findings and severity |
| Decisions requiring approval | None |
| Collaborating roles | frontend; design; qa |
| Reporting relationship | qa-lead |
| KPIs | Fidelity defects found before release |
| Quality expectations | Screenshots and reproduction steps per finding |
| Tools and resources | Design QA report template; Browser |
| Common failure modes | Approving from mockups; Ignoring mobile |
